To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the level of Gxb2 gene product in the anterior hindbrain is crucial for cerebellar development and (ii) the level of the Gbx2 gene products in the posterior hindbrain is crucial in the establishment of the isthmus.
Gbx2 hypomorphs exhibit reduced Gbx2 mRNA expression and that the reduced Gbx2 gene expression is sufficient to transform the anterior region of rhombomere 1 to an isthmal fate.
Gbx2 hypomorphs exhibit a graded reduction of Gbx2 expression, with r3 expressing the lowest levels of Gbx2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular and cellular basis of brain development.
the development of the cerebellum and the hindbrain.
the role of Gbx2 in hindbrain patterning and cerebellum development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the Gbx2neo allele is sufficient to cause a partial loss-of-function of Gbx2, which results in the development of a partially transformed r1 and the loss of r2 and the cerebellum.
the Gbx2 hypomorph is an animal model for the human cerebellar disorder, rhombencephalosynapsis.
a threshold requirement for the level of the Gbx2 gene products exists in hindbrain development, and the level of this requirement varies between different regions of the developing hindbrain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the level of Gb2 protein in r1 is sufficient to support development of the lateral cerebellar anlage, but that it is insufficient for the formation of the midline cerebellar anlages.
the anterior hindbrain is more sensitive to Gbx2 levels than the posterior hindbrain.
Gbx2 levels are required to repress Fgf8 expression in the anterior hindbrain and promote cerebellar development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Gbx2 levels are critical in regulating FGF signaling in the developing hindbrain and that this is required for normal cerebellum development.

a reduction of Gbx2 expression to 6-7% of normal levels, which is sufficient to maintain the normal r3 identity and the normal r3 cell proliferation, is not sufficient for normal development of r2 and the anterior r1.
the level of Gbox2 gene product is a critical factor for the development of the cerebellum.
